output.brief: FCR fell because of Finance's 14 April change, not the new starters. It cut agents' in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically sends larger billing adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred jumped from 7% to 54% that same week, and referred calls resolve at about 34% versus 82% for the rest. Referral rates and the FCR drop are the same across April-intake, mid-tenure and long-tenured agents. Tariff-enquiry mix shifted but that group still resolves at 85%. So the new-starter explanation, tariff mix and performance plans are not supported, and plans would punish the wrong people. I'm fairly confident, although I didn't check the IVR or workload data directly. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Add post-call sampling, and track FCR and unsupported credits. Finance requires that kind of trial before it will raise the limit. Don't put the April intake on performance plans, and don't roll out a higher limit everywhere at once. Pausing the IVR work isn't justified by this evidence. MI can rerun the breakdown for the trial teams within a day, so the full dashboard rebuild isn't needed to start.
